newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Agriculture commodities push NZ Sept qtr PPI up.
newsitem.headline: Agriculture commodities push NZ Sept qtr PPI up.

text.p: An increase in agricultural commodity prices, particularly sheep and lamb, drove New Zealand output prices higher in the September quarter, Statistics New Zealand said on Tuesday.
Output price levels of goods and services sold by New Zealand industries rose on average by 0.4 percent in the September quarter, following a 0.2 percent fall in the June quarter.
Output prices for the September quarter were 0.5 percent higher than those a year ago.
SNZ said the agriculture outputs index rose 3.5 percent in the September quarter, with rising sheep and lamb livestock prices the main contributor.
"This follows increases in sheep and lamb meat prices in world markets, particularly Britain," SNZ said.
Deer livestock prices rose, following record venison prices on world markets. Wool prices increased slightly, as did beef prices.
The food, beverages and tobacco index rose 1.8 percent in the quarter, providing the second biggest contribution to the rise in the outputs index.
Forestry and logging, down 2.4 percent due to lower export log prices, provided the main offset to the increase.

Input price levels of goods and services, excluding wages and depreciation, purchased by New Zealand industries rose on average by 0.2 percent in the quarter, following a 0.2 percent fall in the June quarter.
In the year to September input price levels rose 0.4 percent.

Higher prices for sheep and lamb livestock contributed the most to the quarterly increase in the inputs index, but this was partially offset by a 1.8 percent fall in the machinery and metals products index.
